mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (below 4.0% historical average) compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in 60% or more of periods when FEDFUNDS < 4.0%, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (exceeding 0.5 percentage points over three months) signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce corporate earnings expectations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in 60% or more of triggered instances (UNRATE rise > 0.5pp in 3 months), or Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) below their 12-month moving averages signal a broad-based consumer demand contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in 60% or more of periods where both HOUST and RSAFS are below 12-month moving averages, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production (more than 1.0% in one month) signals a supply shock that disrupts corporate operations and reduces earnings, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in 60% or more of triggered instances (INDPRO fall > 1.0% in 1 month), or Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Strong monthly payroll growth (PAYEMS exceeding 0.5% year-over-year) indicates expanding labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in 60% or more of months with PAYEMS growth > 0.5% (y/y), or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL exceeding 3.0% year-over-year) triggers expectations of monetary tightening, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in 60% or more of months with CPIAUCSL > 3.0% (y/y), or Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 2.0%) signals an active monetary easing cycle that supports risk asset valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in 60% or more of periods where FEDFUNDS declines and CPIAUCSL < 2.0%, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A recession (defined as two consecutive quarters of declining real GDP, GDPC1) signals economic contraction that reduces corporate profits, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in 60% or more of recession periods (two consecutive quarters of GDPC1 decline), or Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.
